system: mixed system of English common law, Islamic law (sharia), and customary law; the Federal Court can review legislative acts at the request of the supreme head of the federation

constitution.history: previous 1948; latest drafted 21 February 1957, effective 27 August 1957
constitution.amend: proposed as a bill by Parliament; passage requires at least two-thirds majority vote by the Parliament membership in the bill's second and third readings; a number of constitutional sections are excluded from amendment or repeal

courts.highest: Federal Court (consists of the chief justice, president of the Court of Appeal, chief justice of the High Court of Malaya, chief judge of the High Court of Sabah and Sarawak, 8 judges, and 1 "additional" judge)
courts.judges: Federal Court justices appointed by the monarch on advice of the prime minister; judges serve until mandatory retirement at age 66 with the possibility of a single 6-month extension
courts.lower: Court of Appeal; High Court; Sessions Court; Magistrates' Court
courts.note: Malaysia has a dual judicial hierarchy of civil and religious (sharia) courts

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must be a citizen of Malaysia

world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; non-party state to the ICCt
